findings.title: Browser identifies itself as headless
findings.explanation: The user agent string and/or the Sec-CH-UA client hint brands advertise a headless browser build.
findings.likely_implications: Sites can distinguish this browser from a normal desktop browser from the first request, before any script runs.
findings.suggested_investigation: Chrome's headless shell (`--headless=old`, Playwright's default chromium_headless_shell) reports HeadlessChrome; new headless mode (`--headless=new`, or Playwright's `channel: 'chromium'`) reports Chrome. Check which headless mode and binary each environment launches.

findings.title: window.chrome is missing in a Chromium browser
evidence: window.chrome is undefined while the CDP product reports a Chromium browser.
findings.explanation: Headed Chrome and new headless mode define window.chrome; the headless shell binary does not.
findings.likely_implications: Scripts that feature-detect Chrome through window.chrome will treat this browser as something else.
findings.suggested_investigation: Check whether the environment runs the headless shell binary rather than the full Chrome/Chromium binary in new headless mode.

findings.title: Plugin list is empty
findings.explanation: Headed Chrome exposes a fixed set of PDF viewer plugins; headless builds expose none.
findings.likely_implications: This may help explain differences between local, Docker, CI, and remote-browser profiles.
findings.suggested_investigation: Compare the same signal across the baseline browser and the candidate browser before treating it as material.

findings.title: Outer window size is zero
findings.explanation: A headed browser window always has a non-zero outer size. Zero outer dimensions indicate a headless or windowless context.
findings.likely_implications: Scripts that compare inner and outer window sizes will classify this browser as headless.
findings.suggested_investigation: Confirm the headless mode in use. New headless mode reports a window size; the headless shell does not.

findings.title: Software WebGL renderer detected
evidence: Renderer evidence: WebKit WebGL SwiftShader Device (Synthetic).
findings.explanation: The WebGL renderer appears to be software-backed rather than normal device GPU rendering.
findings.likely_implications: Rendering hashes and graphics capability may differ materially from a desktop browser baseline.
findings.suggested_investigation: Software rendering is normal in headless, Docker, and CI without a GPU, and is forced by --disable-gpu. Check the launch flags and whether a GPU is available in the candidate environment.

findings.title: No common fonts detected
evidence: None of 31 common fonts rendered differently from the generic fallback families.
findings.explanation: The environment appears to have no commonly installed fonts. Text falls back to whatever the system provides, which is often a single generic face or missing glyphs.
findings.likely_implications: Screenshots, layout metrics, and text-dependent rendering will differ from a desktop baseline, and some sites treat an empty font set as a non-standard environment.
findings.suggested_investigation: Check the container or CI image for installed fonts (for example `fc-list`). Minimal Docker images frequently ship none.

findings.title: IndexedDB is unavailable
findings.explanation: The profile could not open a basic IndexedDB database on the probed page.
findings.likely_implications: Applications that rely on browser storage may fail or behave differently in this environment.
findings.suggested_investigation: Check browser policy, incognito-like modes, and origin/storage restrictions in the candidate environment.

findings.title: Notification permission is denied by default
evidence: Notification.permission is denied on a fresh page.
findings.explanation: A fresh headed Chrome profile reports Notification.permission as default (prompt). Headless Chrome reports denied without any user interaction.
findings.likely_implications: This is a well-known headless indicator, and notification-dependent features will not prompt.
findings.suggested_investigation: Confirm the headless mode in use, or whether a policy or context option denies notifications in the candidate environment.

findings.title: No Accept-Language header is sent
evidence: The browser's request for the diagnostic page carried no Accept-Language header.
findings.explanation: Every headed browser sends Accept-Language. A missing header usually means the browser was launched with no locale configured, which happens with the headless shell and some minimal containers.
findings.likely_implications: Sites that negotiate language, currency, or region from Accept-Language will serve different content than the baseline, and some treat the missing header as a non-browser client.
findings.suggested_investigation: Set a locale on the context (Playwright `locale`, Puppeteer `--lang`/`--accept-lang`) or in the container environment, matching the baseline.
